context.alert_text: More than one deployment in progress on the API service for 15 minutes

root_cause.hypothesis: The pipeline pushed three task-definition revisions to warden-dev-api within about an hour (07:03, 07:31, 07:58), and the latest deploy (D1) was already an automatic rollback from revision 44 back to 41/image 7.2.4. The overlapping/retried deployments produced failed tasks and left two deployments in flight, which is what is tripping the DeploymentCount>1 alarm, even though current running/desired task counts look healthy.
ruled_out: Networking/security-group change: C9 unchanged, no CHANGE items reference the SG.
Resource exhaustion: M7/M8 CPU and memory are within normal range.

proposal.reasoning: Three rapid deploys in under an hour, culminating in an automatic rollback from revision 44 to 41 and still showing deployments_in_flight=2 with 1 failed deployment and 6 failed tasks, indicate the pipeline is retrying/oscillating deploys faster than the service can stabilize. Freezing further deploys on warden-dev-api lets the current (rolled-back) revision settle and prevents another overlapping deployment from re-triggering the DeploymentCount alarm or masking the real failure in the new image.
proposal.expected_effect: No new task-definition deploys are accepted for warden-dev-api until a human clears the freeze, allowing the already-stable running tasks (4/4) to remain and the deployment counters to drain back to a single completed deployment.

reasons: Passed all policies. Held for operator approval before execution.
